title: Staff notation
examples: How many lines are on the staff?
What is the treble clef for?
Can you show me a note on a ledger line?

explain.say: Today we are learning about staff notation for music.
First we look at the clef which tells us the pitch.
The lines themselves have special names for notes.

draw.text: Line names: E G B D F

explain.say: The spaces also have their own easy to remember names.

draw.text: Space names: F A C E

explain.say: Sometimes notes go below or above the lines.
For example, a note written on a ledger line below the staff is low.

faq.q: What is the difference between a clef and a note name?
faq.a: The clef tells you which pitch level the staff represents. The note name is the specific pitch written on the lines or spaces.
asks: How do I read the pitch?
Is the clef the same as the note?

faq.q: Do I need to know the names of the lines and spaces?
faq.a: Knowing the names helps you read music accurately. It gives you a reliable system for identifying pitches.
asks: What are the notes on the lines?
What are the notes in the spaces?
Is there a pattern for the notes?

faq.q: When do I use ledger lines?
faq.a: You use ledger lines when the note is too high or too low for the five lines. They extend the staff to show these extra pitches.
asks: What if a note is really high?

faq.q: Does the clef change the note name?
faq.a: The clef sets the key for the entire piece of music. It determines what the notes on the lines and spaces actually sound like.
asks: Why do we need different clefs?
What if I mix up the clefs?

faq.q: Are there specific notes for every line?
faq.a: Yes, the lines and spaces follow a pattern. For example, the lines in the treble clef spell E G B D F.
asks: What are the notes on the staff lines?
Can you remember the line names?
Is there a mnemonic for the notes?

facts: A standard musical staff has five parallel lines.
The treble clef is commonly used for higher-pitched instruments.
The notes on the lines of the treble clef are E, G, B, D, and F.
Ledger lines are added to extend the range of notes above or below the staff.

quiz.say: If a note is written on the third line of the staff, what is its name?
quiz.why: The third line always represents the note B in the treble clef.

wrong.1: D is actually on the fourth line, which is a common mix-up.
wrong.2: G is on the second line, making it an easy mistake to switch.
wrong.3: A is in the second space, not on the third line.

quiz.say: What does the bass clef primarily indicate?
quiz.why: The bass clef is designed to read the lower sounding notes of music.

wrong.1: High pitch is usually shown using the treble clef.
wrong.2: The clef tells you pitch, not just how long the note lasts.
wrong.3: Tempo is indicated by separate markings, not the clef.
